text:
Ah, Christopher Columbus. The true pioneer of the 15th century, who looked at the vast, uncharted ocean and said, "You know what this world needs? More land, but let’s pretend I discovered it for the first time." A visionary, truly.

But let us not dwell on the past, for the present offers us a far more thrilling spectacle of human ingenuity. Behold the modern marvel: the "New and Improved" version of the exact same object you bought last year. It is not merely a product; it is a philosophical statement. Why settle for a blue phone when you can have a "Midnight Blue" phone that costs $200 more? The audacity is breathtaking. The creativity? Off the charts.

We are living in an age where consumers are so brilliantly gullible that they will happily pay a premium for the privilege of being told they need something they already possess. It is not marketing; it is a social experiment in mass delusion. And the best part? They thank you for it. They line up around the block, eyes wide with wonder, ready to exchange their hard-earned cash for the same old thing, now dressed in a sleek adjective like "Pro," "Ultra," or "Next-Gen."

It is truly inspiring to watch us all play along. After all, if we don’t buy the new color, who will? The old one? Please. That’s so last season.
